issues.legal_issue: Whether the required local publication of an acquisition notification occurred.
material_facts: The acquisition authority filed an affidavit stating that the substance of the notification had been announced in the affected localities.
Landowners filed objections after the announcements, and the landowners challenging the acquisition did not dispute that those objections had been filed.
The objection petitions contained notes recording the announcements in the villages.
issues.conclusion: The Court found that the substance of the notification had been published in the localities and rejected the challenge based on alleged non-publication.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 requires public notice of the substance of the notification at convenient places in the locality. Whether that requirement was met is preeminently a question of fact; the evidence of publication and the ensuing objections established publication here.

predicates.acquisition_challenge: The affected owners challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.official_evidence_of_local_announcement: The acquisition authority provided evidence that it announced the substance of the proposed acquisition in the affected locality.
predicates.landowners_filed_objections_after_announ: Affected owners filed objections to the proposed acquisition after the announcement.

issues.definition: When an acquisition is challenged and the authority provides evidence of a local announcement followed by objections from affected owners, local publication is established.

issues.legal_issue: Whether an acquisition for development and industrialisation is invalid because the acquiring authority later transfers the land to another agency or allegedly makes a profit.
material_facts: The land was acquired for development and industrialisation for industrial use, a public purpose the challengers did not contest.
The acquiring development authority transferred the land to an industrial development corporation after undertaking external development, and the corporation undertook internal development.
The challengers relied on the transfer and payment for the land to allege profiteering but provided no supporting facts or evidence in their pleadings.
The Court stated that even if the development authority had made some profit, that would not affect the public purpose or invalidate the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the profiteering challenge; transfer to another agency for development and even the making of some profit did not invalidate the acquisition for the unchallenged public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Development and industrialisation can constitute a public purpose, and the acquiring authority may carry out development through another agency. The Court distinguished the amended definition discussed in Arnold Rodricks v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1966 SC 1788, because the provision before it did not contain that amendment, and did not adopt the minority observation there as controlling. It also rejected reliance on State of Bihar v. Maharajadhiraja Sir Kameshwar Singh, [1952] 3 SCR 889, as not establishing that this acquisition was a profiteering venture. Under the unamended section 3(f) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, alleged profit does not by itself defeat an otherwise unchallenged public purpose.

rule.if: acquisition_challenge and stated_purpose_is_development and stated_public_purpose_is_unchallenged and land_transferred_for_development

predicates.acquisition_challenge: Affected owners challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.stated_purpose_is_development: The acquiring authority stated that the land was being acquired to develop it for a public use.
predicates.stated_public_purpose_is_unchallenged: The affected owners did not challenge the stated development purpose as a public purpose.
predicates.land_transferred_for_development: The acquiring authority transferred the land to another agency for further development or use consistent with the stated purpose.

issues.definition: If affected owners challenge an acquisition for an unchallenged development purpose and the land is transferred for that development, the transfer or alleged profit alone does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a factual ground presented as a point of law may be entertained in a writ proceeding when its supporting facts and evidence are not pleaded and produced.
material_facts: The challengers alleged that the acquisition was a profiteering venture, a contention that required supporting facts.
Their writ petitions and affidavits did not set out and support the necessary facts and evidence; they sought to rely at the hearing on statements in another agency's application.
The Court held that the ground was not entertainable on that basis, although it also considered and rejected the ground on its merits.
issues.conclusion: A fact-dependent legal ground unsupported by pleaded facts and evidence in the writ petition or counter-affidavit will not be entertained; the Court nevertheless considered this ground and found it meritless.
issues.legal_principle: A writ petitioner raising a point that appears to be one of law but requires factual substantiation must plead the relevant facts and provide the supporting evidence in the writ petition. A respondent must do so in the counter-affidavit. Unlike pleadings under the Code of Civil Procedure, a writ petition or counter-affidavit must set out both the facts and the evidence supporting them.

predicates.writ_proceeding: A party raises a ground in a writ proceeding.
predicates.fact_dependent_legal_ground: The party presents a purported legal point whose resolution depends on factual substantiation.
predicates.supporting_facts_or_evidence_not_pleaded: The party does not set out the relevant facts and supporting evidence in the writ petition or counter-affidavit.

issues.definition: In a writ proceeding, a fact-dependent legal ground will not be entertained if the party has not pleaded its supporting facts and evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a development agency that receives acquired land for development becomes the acquiring authority, requiring compliance with procedures applicable to acquisition for a company.
material_facts: The acquisition notification stated that a public development authority would undertake the development and industrialisation of the land.
That authority later transferred the land to an industrial corporation for development and allotment to others.
The challengers argued that the corporation was the true acquiring authority and that procedures applicable to acquisition for a company had not been followed.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the public development authority was the acquiring authority and that the later transfer to the corporation for development did not make the corporation the acquiring authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(e) and Part III of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the identity of the acquiring authority is not changed merely because that authority transfers acquired land to another agency for development and allotment. The acquiring authority may develop the land itself or through other agencies; the notification identified the public development authority as the authority responsible for the acquisition and development.

predicates.acquisition_challenge: Affected owners challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.public_authority_identified_as_acquirer: The acquisition notice identified a public authority as the body acquiring the land for the stated public development purpose.
predicates.land_transferred_to_company_for_developm: The public authority transferred the land to a company or other agency for development or allotment after acquisition.

issues.definition: When the acquisition notice identifies a public authority as the acquirer and that authority later transfers the land to a company for development, the public authority remains the acquiring authority.

issues.legal_issue: Whether acquiring suitable land for a public purpose is discriminatory merely because land belonging to other people was not acquired.
material_facts: The challengers said that land belonging to other people in the village had not been acquired.
The Court considered the selected land to have been acquired because it was suitable for the stated public purpose.
The Court stated that the government would acquire only the land necessary and suitable for that purpose.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the discrimination claim based solely on the fact that other people's land had not been acquired.
issues.legal_principle: The government may acquire the amount of land necessary and suitable for the public purpose in question. Selection of suitable land does not, by itself, establish discrimination merely because other land was left unacquired.

predicates.acquisition_challenge: Affected owners challenged the selection of land for a public acquisition.
predicates.selected_land_found_suitable_for_public_: The acquired land was considered suitable for the stated public purpose.
predicates.other_land_not_acquired: The challengers pointed out that land belonging to other people was not acquired.

issues.definition: If selected land is suitable for the public purpose, the fact that other land was not acquired does not alone establish discrimination.

issues.legal_issue: Whether acquisition of agricultural land for industrial development is invalid when the government is alleged not to have considered a policy calling for restraint in acquiring land.
material_facts: The challengers relied on a government policy calling for restraint in acquiring land for development activities and argued that agricultural land should not have been acquired.
The Court recognized the need to balance agricultural needs against development and industrialisation.
The allegation that the government had failed to consider the need for agricultural land was vague and unsupported by material.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge because the allegation of failure to consider the relevant needs was vague and unsupported, and the state had to balance agricultural needs against development and industrialisation.
issues.legal_principle: A government must balance the need to preserve agricultural land against the need for development and industrialisation, which the Court described as part of the state's responsibility to promote progress and address unemployment. A bare allegation that the government failed to consider that balance, without supporting material, does not establish invalidity.

predicates.acquisition_challenge: Affected owners challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_for_industrial_development: The land was acquired for development and industrial use.
predicates.unsupported_allegation_of_failure_to_con: The challengers alleged that the government failed to consider agricultural needs but provided no material supporting that allegation.

issues.definition: When affected owners challenge an industrial development acquisition on the basis of an unsupported claim that agricultural needs were not considered, that challenge is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Whether an owner who becomes landless through acquisition must receive an allotment of developed land.
material_facts: The affected owners asked for developed land so that those rendered landless by acquisition could establish businesses and earn a livelihood.

The Court directed the industrial development corporation to consider an application from an affected person who had genuinely become landless and to give that person priority if the person met the allotment conditions and a plot was available.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the corporation to consider an application from a person rendered landless and give that person priority in allotment if the person qualified and a plot was available; it did not guarantee an allotment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court's direction was conditional: an affected person who genuinely became landless could apply, and the allotment authority was to consider the application and give priority only if the applicant fulfilled the conditions and a plot was available.

rule.if: acquisition_proceeding and person_rendered_landless and application_for_allotment_made and applicant_meets_conditions and plot_available

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns a proceeding challenging a land acquisition.
predicates.person_rendered_landless: A person lost all of their land as a result of the acquisition.
predicates.application_for_allotment_made: The person rendered landless applied to the allotment authority for developed land.
predicates.applicant_meets_conditions: The applicant fulfilled the conditions required for allotment.
predicates.plot_available: A plot was available for allotment.

issues.definition: If acquisition renders a person landless and that person applies, qualifies, and a plot is available, the application must be considered with priority.

issues.legal_issue: Whether land containing a place of worship, a public water facility, or a rest house should be exempted from acquisition.
material_facts: The challengers asserted that acquired land included a temple, a public water facility, and a rest house.
They asked the Court to exempt that land from acquisition.
The Court declined to issue an exemption direction but left them free to make a representation to the relevant authority.
issues.conclusion: The Court issued no direction exempting the land from acquisition and permitted the challengers to make a representation to the relevant authority.
issues.legal_principle: On the material presented, the Court did not consider it necessary to direct an exemption and left the issue for a representation to the authority concerned.

predicates.acquisition_challenge: Affected owners challenged the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.structures_claimed_on_acquired_land: The owners asserted that the acquired land contained community or religious structures.
predicates.no_basis_established_for_court_order: The owners did not establish a basis for the Court to direct that the land be exempted.

issues.definition: When owners claim that structures lie on acquired land but establish no basis for a court-ordered exemption, no exemption direction is made, though they may seek relief by representation.
